## TL;DR

Review round 1 found one real defect with a wide reach: the shared markdown parser ended a list item at its first unmarked line, so wrapped bullets split into a list, a stray paragraph and another list. The same parser cut a blockquote short on a lazy continuation line. Both are fixed in `src/ui-app/src/lib/markdown.ts`, and every consumer of `renderMarkdown` and `renderChatMarkdown` gets the fix. I also addressed the review's suggestions and removed two alias tokens that were overriding designed fallback colours. The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes after the final edit, including remote validation.

## Work and rationale

**List continuation (the review's main finding).** `parseBlocks` consumed only lines that matched the list marker. An indented continuation line or an unmarked lazy line therefore ended the list. I changed the item collector: each item now gathers its indented body (content column = marker width), plus CommonMark lazy continuation lines (unmarked text right after a paragraph line). The body is parsed as blocks, so nested sub-lists stay nested. A blank line keeps a list open only when the next marker follows it, so loose lists become one `ul`/`ol` rather than several. The item type is now `{ checked, lines, children }`, and `renderItemBody` renders the paragraph and any children inside the `li`.

**Blockquote lazy lines.** The quote loop now takes an unmarked, non-blank line that follows a paragraph line. A blank line still ends the quote. My first version treated the blank line as lazy and added a trailing space and an empty line. That was caught by the existing `renders blockquotes and horizontal rules` test.

**Progress guard.** The paragraph loop could consume nothing when its first line matched a paragraph-break pattern without a block dispatcher claiming it (a bare `# ` does this). It now takes that line as text, so the loop always advances.

**Designed fallbacks.** I aliased `--warning` and `--yellow` to `--amber`. Both were read elsewhere with designed fallback colours (`#987029`, `#e6b450`), which the aliases would have overridden. I removed both aliases and pointed the unfallbacked reads at `--amber` directly (TaskCard, ServiceSettings, ScheduledTasksPanel). The guard then caught a dead inner read in DebugPanel, which I also fixed.

**Review suggestions.** `docs-reader-qa-browser.test.ts` now throws if the built global stylesheet is older than `src/style.css`, so a stale build fails loudly. I removed the permanently undeclared `--warn` leg from ScheduledTasksPanel.

**Shot.** The first declared shot highlighted `.tree-file.sel`, which is inside a collapsed folder on that route, so it matched nothing. It now highlights `.doc-title`, which renders once a document is open.

## Approaches tried

- A first pass of the list fix let a lazy line continue only after a non-empty body line. Reproducing `- first bullet` then `lazy continuation` showed the list still breaking, because the first line has no body yet. The rule now also accepts a lazy line when the item's first line has text.
- `sed` could not do the import edit because of shell quoting, so I used the edit tool.
- My first `repoos check` run hit my own 590-second timeout while browser tests were still running. That is a timeout on my side, not a failure. I reran the check in the background to completion.

## Challenges and blockers

- The earlier draft was consumed by RepoOS on the passing handoff, so this round's draft covers only the review fixes.
- The review's Dropdowns example is reproduced and now renders as one item. I checked the output by running the real module, not only through unit tests.

## Key learnings

- A parser change that is correct for one consumer can break several. I checked each consumer's suite (markdown, docs reader, story panel, chat, debugger, schedule and card suites) rather than one file.
- A fallback colour in a `var()` is a design decision. An alias that matches the name but not the intent silently replaces it. Before aliasing a name, check whether it is read with a fallback.
